description: Vizro is a low-code toolkit for building high-quality data visualization apps.

summary.one_liner: Vizro is an open-source, low-code Python toolkit for building multi-page data visualization dashboards defined by configuration rather than extensive code.
summary.what_it_does: Vizro lets you assemble data visualization apps from a small set of high-level configuration categories: components (charts, tables, cards, KPI indicators, forms), controls (filters and parameters such as drop-downs and sliders), actions (interactions between components, drill-throughs, export), layouts (grid or flexible containers with preset styles), and navigation (including nested page hierarchies). Configuration can be written as Pydantic models, JSON, YAML, or Python dictionaries. Optional high-code extensions allow custom visual formatting and custom components using Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS. The framework is built on Plotly, Dash, and Pydantic. The monorepo also contains vizro-ai and vizro-mcp, an MCP server that helps LLM clients such as Cursor or Claude Desktop build Vizro dashboards and charts.
use_cases: Prototype BI-style dashboards that can be deployed to production
Create interactive charts with filters and drill-throughs
Generate dashboards from YAML or JSON configuration
Choose chart types using a visual vocabulary
Use an AI assistant to build Vizro dashboards
notable: Low-code configuration via Pydantic models, JSON, YAML, or Python dictionaries
Built-in visual design best practices for default styling
Optional high-code extensions for custom components and formatting
Vizro-MCP server for LLM-assisted dashboard creation
Visual vocabulary of chart examples with sample Plotly code
caveats: Custom components and bespoke formatting require high-code extensions
Upgrading from 0.1.x involves breaking changes covered in a migration guide
